# Parallax bias of the straight-line motion fit (generated by `scripts/parallax_effect.py`)

Cold Movers fits a straight line (proper motion only) to positions measured at each SPHEREx visit. Parallax adds a yearly ellipse to the real path. This table fits the same straight line to the parallax displacement alone, at each object's own visit dates, so the slope is the bias parallax adds to the measured motion. Catalogue parallaxes; the Sun's position from the Astronomical Almanac's low-precision formula.

| Object | Parallax | Visits (span) | Largest parallax shift between visits | Bias on the fitted motion | Bias in pixels per year | Compared with the measured − catalogue difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Barnard's Star | 547.0 mas | 6 (1.07 yr) | 1.09″ (0.18 px) | 0.11″/yr | 0.018 | fitted 10.69 ± 0.76 vs catalogue 10.39″/yr: difference +0.30″/yr |
| Epsilon Indi B | 270.7 mas | 4 (1.41 yr) | 0.52″ (0.08 px) | 0.19″/yr | 0.030 | fitted 4.59 ± 0.69 vs catalogue 4.68″/yr: difference -0.09″/yr |
| R Draconis | 1.3 mas | 3 (1.00 yr) | 0.00″ (0.00 px) | 0.00″/yr | 0.000 | no trajectory fit (slower than 0.5″/yr) |
| RW Aurigae | 6.4 mas | 3 (1.01 yr) | 0.01″ (0.00 px) | 0.00″/yr | 0.000 | no trajectory fit (slower than 0.5″/yr) |
| TRAPPIST-1 | 80.2 mas | 3 (1.00 yr) | 0.16″ (0.03 px) | 0.00″/yr | 0.000 | fitted 1.06 ± 1.04 vs catalogue 1.05″/yr: difference +0.01″/yr |
| WISE 0855-0714 | 439.0 mas | 4 (0.99 yr) | 0.88″ (0.14 px) | 0.10″/yr | 0.017 | fitted 9.18 ± 1.87 vs catalogue 8.15″/yr: difference +1.03″/yr |

Reading: when the bias is comparable with the measurement uncertainty, the straight-line motion of that object should not be over-interpreted; modelling parallax needs more visits spread over the year (SPHEREx returns about every six months, so most objects have 3-6 visits).
